en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga,
Chapter on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Surusuru Chapter 57.
The Training Rule on Holding an Umbrella.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks were teaching the Dhamma to one holding a sunshade.
Those monks who were of few desires... [as before]... complained, grumbled, and became indignant, saying:
"How can the group-of-six monks teach the Dhamma to one holding a sunshade?"... [as before]...
“Is it true, monks, that you teach the Dhamma to one who holds a sunshade?
“It is true, Blessed One.
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them... [as before] ...
"How indeed, you foolish men, can you teach the Dhamma to one with a sunshade in hand?
This, foolish men, will not lead to the confidence of those without confidence...
And furthermore, monks, you should recite this training rule as follows:"
“The training is to be observed: ‘I shall not teach the Dhamma to one with a sunshade in hand.
Thus was this training rule laid down by the Blessed One for the bhikkhus.
Now at that time, the bhikkhus were anxious to teach the Dhamma to one who was ill and carrying a sunshade.
People complained, grumbled, and spread it about:
“How can these ascetics, followers of the Sakyan, refuse to teach the Dhamma to one who is sick and carrying a sunshade?
The monks heard those people complaining, grumbling, and spreading it about.
Then those bhikkhus reported this matter to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One, having given a discourse on the Dhamma with reference to this cause and this occasion, addressed the bhikkhus:
“I allow you, bhikkhus, to teach the Dhamma to one who is sick while holding a sunshade.”
And so, monks, you should recite this training rule:
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall not teach the Dhamma to one who has a sunshade in hand and is not ill.
As for "a sunshade": [it is as follows].
There are three kinds of umbrellas: a white umbrella, a palm-leaf umbrella, and a leaf umbrella bound with rings or bound with strips of wood.
What is called "Dhamma" is that spoken by the Buddha, spoken by disciples, spoken by seers, or spoken by deities; it is endowed with meaning and endowed with the Dhamma.
If he teaches by means of the word "deseyya," there is an offense of wrong-doing for every single word.
If he teaches by means of the syllables, there is an offense of wrong-doing for every single syllable.
The Dhamma should not be taught to one who is not ill and is holding a sunshade.
Whoever, out of disrespect, teaches the Dhamma to one who is not ill and is holding a sunshade, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense—
"Unintentionally... [as before] ...for one who is a first-time offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
